name: Add Values to an Empty List (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that creates a list of eight string values received from the user.
code:
#Step 1: Create an empty list
lst = []
#Step 2: Add the user inputs to the list one by one
for i in range(8):
    lst.append( input("Enter a value:") ) 
#Step 3: Print the list
print(lst)

commentList: We need to create a list of the user inputs. Therefore, we initialize the list referred by variable lst with an empty list and will later use the function append to add user inputs to it.

3.content: #Step 2: Add the user inputs to the list one by one

commentList: We use a for loop to repeat receiving the user input eight times and add each input to the list. We repeat the for loop eight times by calling the function range(8).

This function will generate a sequence of numbers that starts at 0 with every integer number up to but not including 8. The for statement iterates over the numbers in this sequence in order, executing the statement inside the loop body for each number.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

We want to add the user input to the list. To do this, in each iteration, we call the function append(input("Enter a value:"). Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from the input function in a variable. We could use the input function call directly as the append function parameter.

The input() function will print the text "Enter a value:" on the screen, reads the text entered by the user and returns it as a string value. The append function uses the value returned by the input() function and adds that to the end of the list.
We can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing list lst to that. This statement will print the list.
